oracle: encode with the mode's encFunc from WolfDec::DefaultCryptModes(), decode with the mode's decFunc, compare every produced path and byte against the owned input tree

vendor.accessor: build/vcpkg/ports/uberwolf/default-crypt-modes.patch (WolfDec::DefaultCryptModes() over the unchanged default table, UberWolfLib/WolfDec.cpp)

mode_3.note: reused, not regenerated: src/tests/fixtures/wolfrpg/classic-dx8-payload.wolf (966 bytes) is the existing mode-3 (Wolf RPG v2.225) golden archive, asserted in src/tests/unit/wolfrpg_adapter.cpp

ver5_stored_body.choice: the two VER5 fixtures (v2.01, v2.10) are frozen exactly as the vendor encoder produced them with Press=false: the mode's default cipher is applied over a stored (uncompressed) body
ver5_stored_body.press_true_issue: the unchanged DXArchive_VER5 compression stage does not terminate with Press=true (bounded at 25-30 s) for both the literal 30-byte and the 8192-byte body; the same EncodeArchive entry point with Press=false returns rc=0 and the unchanged VER5 decoder round-trips the output to the exact input tree, isolating the failure to the VER5 compression stage and leaving the VER5 container/cipher path intact
ver5_stored_body.scope: the compression codec itself is exercised by the other default modes (which carry vendor default Press=true bodies) and by the LZ/Huffman suites; no variant is required to round-trip through a compressed body, so the stored-body choice does not weaken this fixture suite

notes: The VER5/VER6 EncodeArchiveOneDirectory entry points over-allocate too small a path list under UNICODE (FileNum*(256+sizeof(TCHAR*)) bytes for FileNum*256 TCHAR), so modes 0/1/2 were driven through the same class's EncodeArchive entry point with a correctly sized list; mode 2 round-trips through the unchanged VER6 encoder/decoder with Press=true, and modes 0/1 round-trip through the unchanged VER5 encoder/decoder with Press=false (see ver5_stored_body).

Modes 0/1/2 were generated in a dedicated pass: out/scratch/wolfrpg-default-modes/bin/gen.exe <scratch> src/tests/fixtures/wolfrpg 0,1 --nopress --all-fixtures for modes 0/1 and the same generator without --nopress for modes 2/4/5/9/10. Each run printed the frozen file_size and file_fnv1a64 shown above.

Byte-identical regeneration is not achievable with the unchanged encoder: it stamps each DARC_FILEHEAD timestamp from the live file system and the OS bumps LastAccess on every read / directory enumeration, so a re-run produces a different (but structurally identical) compressed blob. The frozen file_size and file_fnv1a64 are the drift control; the decoded payloads are content-deterministic and are re-verified on every oracle run.
Only each entry's unpacked size and bytes are frozen. The encoded physical extent (stored_size) depends on the vendor container/press layout and is deliberately not re-derived here.
